cases.answerText:
Under the 2022 NYC Mechanical Code, equipment and appliances that are part of building mechanical systems regulated by the code must have condensate drains when they contain evaporators or cooling coils. The exception is specifically for evaporators and cooling coils designed to operate in sensible cooling only and not support condensation. Condensate from covered coils and evaporators must run from the drain-pan outlet to an approved disposal place, with at least 1/8 unit vertical per 12 units horizontal (1% slope) toward discharge; it must not discharge into a street, alley, or other area so as to cause a nuisance (MC §§ 301.1, 307.2, 307.2.1).

- **Materials and ordinary pipe size:** The listed materials are cast iron, galvanized steel, copper, cross-linked polyethylene, polyethylene, ABS, CPVC, or PVC pipe or tubing. Components must suit the installation’s pressure and temperature ratings. Condensate waste and drain lines must be at least 3/4-inch internal diameter and must not decrease in size from the drain-pan connection to the disposal place. Joints and connections must follow the applicable NYC Plumbing Code Chapter 7 provisions for the material type (MC § 307.2.2).
- **Short tubing alternative:** Polypropylene tubing may be used in lengths no greater than 12 inches (304.8 mm) for an individual drain application (MC § 307.2.2).
- **Manifolded drains:** Where drains from more than one unit are manifolded, the pipe or tubing must be sized under Table 307.2.2 by its stated equipment-capacity band:

| Equipment capacity | Minimum condensate pipe diameter |
|---|---:|
| Up to 20 tons of refrigeration | 3/4 inch |
| Over 20 to 40 tons | 1 inch |
| Over 40 to 90 tons | 1 1/4 inches |
| Over 90 to 125 tons | 1 1/2 inches |
| Over 125 to 250 tons | 2 inches |

The text does not expressly say whether “equipment capacity” for a multi-unit manifold means the sum of the connected units’ capacities. Also, where multiple evaporators and/or condensate pumps discharge into the same piping system, that piping must prevent condensate from one appliance discharging into another (MC §§ 307.2.2, 307.2.6).

**No.** For a manifolded drain serving equipment with a combined capacity of 30 tons, the table’s “over 20 tons to 40 tons” row requires a minimum **1-inch** pipe; a 3/4-inch internal diameter is undersized. (2022 NYC MC § 307.2.2, Table 307.2.2)
No. With one unit remaining, the table rule for drains from more than one unit manifolded together no longer applies. The separate minimum is **3/4-inch internal diameter**. (2022 NYC MC § 307.2.2)

Under the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code, the ordinary test pressure is at least **1½ times the proposed maximum working pressure, and never less than 3 psig**. If test pressure exceeds 125 psig, it also must not produce hoop stress above 50% of the pipe’s specified minimum yield strength. The section’s exceptions set special pressure and, in some cases, duration rules; the required test medium and test procedure are stated separately. (FGC § 406.4.1)

- **Distribution pressure above 5 psig:** Test at **twice the maximum allowable operating pressure, but not less than 100 psig, for at least 1 hour**. (FGC § 406.4.1)
- **Public corridors:** Gas piping installed **in accordance with § 404** must be tested and proven tight at **10 psig for at least 30 minutes**. Whether a particular installation meets the § 404 condition cannot be determined from the text provided. (FGC § 406.4.1)
- **Meter piping:** Follow the serving utility’s pressure-test requirements. Those requirements must either match the section’s requirements for distribution piping or, if different, the utility must certify that the piping was tested in compliance with its requirements. (FGC § 406.4.1)
- **Coated or wrapped pipe:** All field-applied or factory-applied coated and wrapped pipe must be tested at **at least 100 psig for at least 60 minutes**. Because this is a minimum, the text does not expressly say that it replaces a higher pressure requirement that may also apply; the interaction where categories overlap is not fully specified in the supplied passage. (FGC § 406.4.1)
- **Medium and timing:** For testing, fill the piping with **air or an inert gas**, isolate the pressure source before taking pressure readings, and measure any required test duration **after the testing medium has stabilized**. The supplied section does not state a general duration for the ordinary test-pressure rule. (FGC § 406.4.1)

**No.** FGC § 406.4.1, Exception 4, says “Notwithstanding the above” and requires all field-applied or factory-applied coated and wrapped pipe to be tested at **at least 100 psig for at least 60 minutes**. The described pipe therefore does not meet either minimum at 3 psig for 30 minutes; the 60 minutes are measured after the testing medium stabilizes. (FGC §§ 401.1, 406.4.1)

The separate factory-coating rule applies to coatings intended to protect against corrosion during shipping and storage; it sets a pressure minimum but no duration. Even if it applies here, it does not reduce the coated-and-wrapped minimum: where different sections specify different requirements, FGC § 102.1 requires the most restrictive. (FGC §§ 406.4.1.1, 102.1)

Under the 2022 NYC Building Code’s ordinary stair rule, a nosing’s curvature or bevel must be **at least 1/16 inch and no more than 9/16 inch**, measured from the tread’s foremost projection. Risers must be solid and vertical, or may slope under the tread above from the underside of the nosing above at an angle **no greater than 30° from vertical** (BC § 1011.5.5). These are separate from the projection rule: the leading edge may project no more than **1¼ inches beyond the tread below** (BC § 1011.5.5.1).

The solid-riser rule has stated exceptions, including certain non-exit or specified occupancies and stair types; the Group R-3 exception also sets a leading-edge radius limit of 9/16 inch. Whether an exception applies depends on the stair’s applicable conditions. (BC § 1011.5.5.3)
No. Under the ordinary 2022 NYC Building Code rule, a riser sloped under the tread above may be no more than 30° from vertical; 35° exceeds that limit by 5° (BC § 1011.5.5).

Under the 2022 NYC Plumbing Code, accessible backwater valves are required where fixtures, floor drains, or area drains are subject to overflow from backwater from the public sewer. A building in a flood hazard area is deemed subject to that overflow and must have valves meeting the additional requirements of ASCE 24 § 7.3.3, as modified by NYC Building Code Appendix G; the supplied text does not establish those referenced requirements, so I cannot describe them further. (PC § 715.1)

The valve may be installed in the fixture drain from the affected fixture, in the branch drain to the affected area drain or group of fixtures, or in the building drain where it exits the building, downstream of the building trap. It must be accessible, with access to its working parts for service and repair. If the centerline of any drain line is 18 inches (457 mm) or more below a slab on grade, a masonry access manhole is required. (PC §§ 715.1, 715.5)

Yes. The 2022 NYC Plumbing Code requires a masonry access manhole when the centerline of any drain line is **18 inches (457 mm) or more** below a slab on grade; exactly 18 inches meets that threshold. (PC § 715.5)

**No.** In the NYC Zoning Resolution text through August 13, 2026, § 37-32 says the minimum depth for required ground-floor non-residential uses, “as applicable,” is set forth in that section, subject to § 37-31; those uses along a designated frontage must extend to the “minimum qualifying depth.” The supplied § 37-32 text gives no universal feet value. (ZR § 37-32.)

Section 37-31 says the provisions of § 37-30, inclusive—including § 37-32—address building frontages in certain areas **not otherwise governed by § 32-30**. It describes them as reference standards for certain streetscape elements applied in conjunction with area-specific requirements under underlying-district regulations, special geographies, or a Special Purpose District. Section 37-31 also excludes the § 37-32 depth requirements for Commercial District zoning lots under 20 feet wide along the street line, only if the lots existed both on March 22, 2016, and on the building-permit application date; and for any community-facility building used exclusively for either a school, or a house of worship, listed under Use Group III(B). The wording leaves unresolved whether “listed under Use Group III(B)” qualifies only the house of worship or both alternatives. (ZR § 37-31.)

For Chapter 6’s covered water-supply systems—those serving human occupancy or habitation and individual water-supply systems—pressure **above 85 psi (586 kPa) static** triggers the requirement. An approved valve conforming to ASSE 1003 or CSA B356, with a strainer, must reduce pressure in the building water-distribution piping to no more than 85 psi static. The exception covers service lines to sill cocks and outside hydrants, and main supply risers where pressure from the mains is reduced to 85 psi or less at individual fixtures. (PC §§ 601.1, 604.8)
